Lesson overview:
- Level: A0 General English
- Unit: Unit 8. People around you
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: What a record!
- Materials: Record cards, stopwatch, superlative cards, COSYmanuals 'can/can't' and 'superlative adjectives' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• describe extreme numerical achievements and world records
• use can for exceptional ability

Quick retrieval task: which words or phrases do you remember?
Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

record — the best result ever. Example: He holds a world record.
top — the highest or best. Example: He is at the top of his class.
best — better than all the others. Example: This is the best present.
fast — moving quickly. Example: He can run fast.
high — far above the ground. Example: The wall is very high.
number — a symbol or amount. Example: What is your phone number?
run — to move quickly on foot. Example: She can run five kilometres.
jump — to move into the air. Example: He can jump very high.
world — the earth and all people. Example: She is famous around the world.
can — a modal verb for ability. Example: I can swim.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• He can run very fast. (describing ability)
• She can jump very high. (describing ability)
• He set a world record. (describing an achievement)
• It is the top record. (describing a record)
• What is the best record? (asking about records)
• How fast can he run? (asking about speed)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'the best result ever'?
Which word means 'the highest or best'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
Pronunciation Focus: The /r/ sound in 'record' and superlative stress

record /ˈrekɔːd/ — stress the first syllable
fast /fɑːst/ — long /ɑː/
high /haɪ/ — long /aɪ/
world /wɜːld/ — one syllable

He can run very fast. She set a world record.

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use 'can' to talk about ability, possibility, and requests; use 'can't' for inability.

Form:
Can / can't: Subject + can + base verb. Negative: cannot / can't. Question: Can you...? Yes, I can. / No, I can't.

Examples:
• I can speak English.
• She can swim very well.
• He can't drive.
• Can you help me?
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
She ___ speak three languages.
I ___ drive a car.
___ you swim?
He can ___ very fast.
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• I can ... (speak / swim / cook).
• I can't ... (drive / dance / sing).
• Can you ...?
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• What can you do well?
• What can't you do?
• Can your best friend cook?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three sentences with 'can' about your abilities.
• Write three sentences with 'can't' about things you cannot do.
Reading: What a record!

What a record! He can run very fast. She can jump very high. He set a world record in 2020. It is the top record in the world. She is the best swimmer in her country. They can achieve amazing things. What is the best record you know? How fast can you run?
What can the man do?
When did he set the record?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: How fast can he run?
B: He can run very fast. He set a world record.
A: What is the record?
B: He is the fastest runner in the world.
A: Can she jump high?
B: Yes, she can. She is the best jumper in her country.
What record did he set?
What is the woman the best at?
Speaking task: Create three class records (fastest, highest, best) and interview your partner about them.

• What world record do you know?
• Can you run fast?
• Can you jump high?
• What is the best record in your country?
• Would you like to set a record?
Role-play: You are a sports reporter. Interview an athlete about their world record.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write five sentences about a record or an exceptional ability.
Model: He/She can ... He/She is the ... in the world.
